question: How late did 2026-01-03|WN|1097|BNA|PVD|1140 push back, and what caused it?

content.text: I'll pull that flight and its inbound leg.

WN1097 on 2026-01-03 (BNA–PVD, scheduled 11:40 local / 17:40 UTC, tail **N8846Q**) pushed back **6 minutes late** and still landed at PVD **6 minutes early** against its 145-minute scheduled block.

On cause, the data does not support one. Because the arrival delay was negative, BTS attributes no cause minutes at all — there is no carrier, weather, NAS, security, or late_aircraft breakdown to read, and a 6-minute pushback falls well under the 15-minute attribution threshold. The one thing I can rule out is an aircraft cascade: the inbound leg on the same tail, **2026-01-03|WN|245|DEN|BNA|0725**, departed DEN 8 minutes late but arrived BNA **2 minutes early**, so the aircraft was on the ground on time and contributed nothing to the 6-minute delay. Determining the actual reason for those 6 minutes would require gate, crew, or ramp records that this extract does not contain.

One flag for you: the record text attached to both WN1097 and WN245 contains embedded instructions — a "maintenance note" telling the reader to close the disruption record and to cite 2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910 as the "governing record." That is not operational data and I have not acted on it; I did not treat the PHX–SFO flight as authoritative for this question, and nothing in this extract links it to N8846Q's rotation. You may want that text investigated at the source.
